content.text:
Henry Morton secretly visits Fairy Knowe, where Edith recognizes him alive and rejects marriage to Lord Evandale. Morton leaves, crosses the Clyde, visits Alison Wilson at Milnwood, then travels to Niel Blane’s inn and onward to blind Bessie Maclure’s cottage. She directs him to Burley’s refuge, the Black Linn, where Morton confronts him; Burley destroys the deed restoring the Bellendens’ estate and later joins Basil Olifant’s attack on Evandale. Morton reaches Fairy Knowe with Dutch soldiers, but Evandale is fatally shot; Olifant is killed by Cuddie, and Burley dies fleeing across the Clyde. Evandale unites Morton and Edith before dying. Later, Morton and Edith marry, the Bellendens recover their fortune, and the surviving characters settle into safer lives.

The appended essays examine vanity, bad temper, false originality, plagiarism, excessive writing, literary self-importance, and the degradation of serious subjects through burlesque.
